text:
mike: spinning up a small canary for orpheus-ptq-v1 (streaming funcall). initial sweep shows ~2.9% json parse failures, concentrated on inputs with emoji or CJK sequences.

anya: can you paste a raw failing output? curious if it's trailing garbage or utf-8 split.

mike: raw snippet: ```{\"action\":\"note\",\"args\":{\"msg\":\"测试失败\uD83D\n\"}}``` ends with broken surrogate and newline. parser errors at EOF.

prajit: runtime token dump shows multibyte emoji split across two stream chunks (high surrogate emitted, low surrogate in next chunk). looks like chunker cuts mid-codepoint under certain int8 kernels.

canary-bot: Canary stats: requests=2000, parse_fail=58 (2.9%), top_error=unexpected end of input, top_tokens=[\"\\uD83D\",\"\\n\",\"\\u201D\"]

anya: propose temporary mitigation: canary-only postprocess `utf8_trim_then_json_repair` that trims tail to last valid utf-8 boundary (max 6 bytes) then runs a tiny json-close heuristic for unmatched braces. enable only for funcall outputs and record telemetry.

mike: implemented branch `ptq-canary-heal` with kill switch config `canary.json_heal=false`. healing order: utf8_trim -> json_close -> retry once if still failing and under retry_budget.

prajit: add guard: only allow healing when top-level keys include `action` and `args` to avoid silently accepting arbitrary payloads. also record original_bytes checksum and healed_bytes checksum for audit.

canary-bot: Deployment: `ptq-canary-heal` enabled at 1719600075

mike: quick smoke: healed 39/58 failures (67%) via utf8_trim, 12 via json_close, 7 remained -> scheduled retry. effective parse_fail ~0.35% on smoke slice. saving healed samples to s3://redwood-canaries/ptq-heal/1719600000/

anya: good interim fix. file ENG-RUNTIME-842 with samples and token dumps for runtime follow-up. keep canary 24h and report final metrics.
